Tourism in Saint Petersburg, the jewel o: A visit to St Petersburg, the jewel of northern Russia, is an experience in itself. The city’s charm lies not only in being Russia’s window on the world but also in being its beating cultural and artistic heart. Founded by Tsar Peter the Great, it has been called the “Venice of the North” thanks to its charming network of canals and elegant bridges, which create an unforgettable romantic scene. St Petersburg is distinguished by its sumptuous palaces, its churches with sparkling golden domes, its wide streets lined with Baroque and neoclassical architecture, and its museums full of priceless treasures.
Visiting this picturesque city is like a: Visiting this picturesque city is like a journey through time, where you can follow in the footsteps of tsars and princes and enjoy the beauty of the Russian arts that have enriched the world. The splendour of Russia is not limited to St Petersburg; it extends to its great capital and many other cities rich in ancient history and unspoilt natural beauty. It is a destination that promises its visitors a unique blend of adventure, culture and experiences that stay etched in the memory. In this comprehensive guide, we look at the highlights of this charming destination, focusing on the most important places to visit in St Petersburg, to help you plan the trip of a lifetime.
Russia is full of many tourist attractio: Russia has a wealth of tourist attractions, from sumptuous palaces and world-class museums to towering cathedrals and stunning landscapes. Because St Petersburg is a central part of the Russian experience, we devote a large part of this section to it, while also highlighting other places that are no less important.

The Winter Palace, which was the residen: The Winter Palace, once the residence of the Russian tsars, and the Hermitage Museum, one of the largest and oldest art museums in the world, are an essential stop on any visit to St Petersburg. The museum holds a huge collection of more than three million works of art and antiquities, spanning ancient times to modern art. Visitors wander through the palace’s stunning halls, viewing masterpieces by Leonardo da Vinci, Rembrandt and other giants of art, as well as the palace rooms decorated with gold and marble that reflect the greatness of the Russian Empire. It is not just a museum; it is a wealth of history and art that speaks for itself.
Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood: Church of the Saviour on Spilled Blood
This stunning church is known as the \"B: This stunning church is also known as the “Church of the Resurrection on the Blood” and is an architectural icon in the heart of St Petersburg. Built on the spot where Emperor Alexander II was assassinated, it is distinguished by its traditional Russian facade and brightly coloured domes, inspired by St Basil’s Cathedral in the capital. Inside, the walls and ceilings are covered with stunning mosaics depicting scenes from the Bible, giving the place an aura of spirituality and breathtaking artistic beauty. It is a masterpiece not to be missed.
Palace of Peter the Great (Peterhof) and: Peterhof (Palace of Peter the Great) and its gardens
Located outside Saint Petersburg, the Pa: Located outside St Petersburg, Peterhof, the palace of Peter the Great, is known as the “Russian Water Gardens” for a splendour and grandeur that rival the world’s greatest palaces. The main palace is distinguished by its magnificent Baroque design, but what makes it unique are its lower and upper gardens, which contain more than 150 fountains, the most famous of which is the “Samson Fountain”, which depicts a lion stalking its prey. The fountains are driven by a unique natural hydraulic system, and the “Dance of the Fountains” is performed daily during the summer, an enchanting spectacle of sight and sound that delights visitors and makes a trip to St Petersburg a complete experience.
Nevsky Prospekt is the main artery of St: Nevsky Prospekt is the main artery of St Petersburg and its beating heart, stretching for more than four kilometres. This lively avenue has a wide range of luxury shops, elegant restaurants, fashionable cafes and famous theatres. Along its length, visitors can admire the beauty of Russian architecture and visit some of the most notable landmarks, such as Kazan Cathedral and the House of Books. It is the perfect place to walk, shop, watch daily city life and see how St Petersburg’s culture of tourism shows around every corner.
St. Isaac's Cathedral is one of the most: St Isaac’s Cathedral is one of the most magnificent cathedrals in Russia, famous for its massive golden dome that dominates the St Petersburg skyline. It took more than 40 years to build and has a lavish neoclassical design, featuring red granite columns and bronze statues. Inside, visitors are dazzled by mosaics and frescoes that cover vast areas. Visitors can climb to the “Colonnade” (the circular walkway) around the cathedral’s dome to enjoy an unrivalled panoramic view of the city and its charming canals.
For art connoisseurs and fans of opera a: For art connoisseurs and fans of opera and ballet, the Mariinsky Theatre in St Petersburg is a global cultural mecca. The theatre has a long history and international fame thanks to the prestigious performances it has staged over the centuries. Enjoy a unique cultural experience and watch classical Russian ballet or world-class opera in a sumptuous setting that reflects the artistic history of the city. A visit to the Mariinsky Theatre is an unforgettable experience and adds a rich cultural dimension to your trip to St Petersburg.
Saint Petersburg is known as the \"Venic: St Petersburg is known as the “Venice of the North” thanks to its extensive network of waterways linking the Neva River with several smaller rivers and canals. Taking a boat ride along these canals is a great way to explore the city from a different perspective and see its historic palaces and bridges. During the White Nights of summer, a unique natural phenomenon when the sun never sets completely, the drawbridges over the Neva River are raised at midnight, an enchanting spectacle that attracts thousands of visitors and shows the magic of St Petersburg at its best.
The Tsar's Village is located a short di: Tsarskoye Selo lies a short distance from St Petersburg and is home to the famous Catherine Palace, which served as the summer residence of the imperial family. It is known for its legendary “Amber Room”, a lavish room decorated entirely with amber panels that glow with a golden light. Although the original room was lost during the war, the reconstructed version remains a masterpiece worth seeing. The palace is surrounded by beautiful, carefully landscaped gardens, making it an ideal place for picnics and for enjoying its historical and natural beauty.
Red Square in the capital is one of the: Red Square in the capital is one of the most famous squares in the world and a symbol of Russia. Beside it stands the Kremlin, a fortified complex of palaces, churches and cathedrals and the official residence of the head of state. Inside the Kremlin, visitors can explore the Transfiguration Cathedral, the Archangel Cathedral and the Armoury Museum, which houses precious imperial treasures. Red Square itself is a living historical site, having witnessed many important events through the ages.
St. Vasily's Cathedral stands tall at th: St Basil’s Cathedral stands tall at the southern end of Red Square and is famous for its unique, colourful domes that resemble rising flames. This cathedral is an icon of Russian architecture, built on the orders of Ivan the Terrible to celebrate his military victories. Its intricate design and bright colours make it one of the most distinctive churches in the world, attracting photographers and visitors from far and wide.
The capital's subway is not only a means: The capital’s metro is not only a means of transport but also an underground art gallery. Many of its stations feature lavish architecture, exquisite artistic details, huge mosaics and stunning sculptures. Some stations are nicknamed “underground palaces” because their beauty rivals that of the finest palaces. A tour of the metro is a unique cultural experience that should not be missed.
The Golden Cities are a group of histori: The Golden Ring is a group of historic cities north-east of the capital that preserve the beauty of old Russian architecture and traditional Orthodox churches. Sergiev Posad, Suzdal and Vladimir are the best known of these cities, offering visitors a glimpse into Russian history and culture away from the hustle and bustle of the big cities. You can explore ancient monasteries and cathedrals decorated with frescoes, and enjoy the tranquillity and charming countryside.
Lake Baikal is the world's largest fresh: Lake Baikal is the world’s largest freshwater lake by volume and depth, and is known as the “Pearl of Russia”. It lies in the eastern part of the country and is famous for its clear turquoise waters, unique biodiversity and the stunning natural scenery that surrounds it. Visitors can take boat trips in summer, or go ice skating and sledging on its frozen surface in winter. It is an ideal destination for nature and adventure lovers.
The city of Sochi, located on the countr: The city of Sochi, on the country’s southern coast, is a popular resort that combines the beauty of warm beaches with the majesty of snowy mountains. The city hosted the Winter Olympics, making it a world-class sports and tourism destination. Visitors can enjoy swimming and relaxing on the beaches in summer, or snowboarding and downhill skiing in winter. It offers a unique mix of leisure activities all year round.
The best time to visit Russia depends on: The best time to visit Russia depends on the type of experience you are looking for, as each season has its own flavour and unique beauty, whether you are planning a trip to St Petersburg or exploring other cities.
Summer is the most popular season to vis: Summer is the most popular season to visit, especially if you want to enjoy pleasant weather and outdoor activities. In St Petersburg, this period brings the magical phenomenon of the “White Nights”, when the sun does not set completely, giving you more time to explore, enjoy the charm of the city and watch the raising of the bridges. The weather is mild and well suited to wandering through parks and palaces and strolling along the banks of the rivers and canals. However, it is also peak season, which means higher prices and crowded tourist sites.
Spring is characterized by the blooming: Spring brings blooming flowers and melting snow, giving the landscape vitality and freshness. The weather is relatively cold at the beginning of spring and gradually improves. This is a good period to visit if you prefer to avoid the large summer crowds and enjoy the beauty of nature at the start of its annual cycle. Museums and parks begin to return to their summer opening hours, making for an enjoyable and relaxed experience.
Autumn presents a stunning sight as tree: Autumn presents a stunning sight as the leaves turn bright gold and red, creating perfect backdrops for photography. The weather is fresh and dry in September, and mild in October before the cold sets in. This season is ideal for cultural visits, as museums are less crowded and theatres and art shows can be enjoyed. It is also a very good time to visit St Petersburg and enjoy its architectural beauty under clear skies and in a calm atmosphere.
For an authentic Russian experience, not: For an authentic Russian experience, nothing beats the beauty of winter. Cities turn into magical snowy worlds, and buildings and landscapes become pure white. Despite the extreme cold, the festive atmosphere of Christmas and New Year adds a special charm. You can go ice skating, visit the winter markets, or simply enjoy the beauty of the cities under a blanket of snow. Indoor attractions such as museums and theatres provide a warm and inviting escape. If you are prepared to brave the cold, winter offers a unique and unforgettable experience.
